newsitem.title: USA: Three Idaho men charged in bombings, bank attacks.
newsitem.headline: Three Idaho men charged in bombings, bank attacks.

text.p: Three north Idaho men believed to be members of an anti-government religious sect were charged with bank robbery and conspiracy Wednesday in connection with a series of pipe bomb attacks in the Spokane area this year.

The three men, arrested at a convenience store by federal and state agents near the central Washington city of Yakima Tuesday, were charged Wednesday in federal court, where at least one indicated he would not cooperate with authorities.

Sandpoint, Idaho, area residents Charles Barbee, 44, Robert Berry, 42, and Jay Merrell, whose age was not given, were charged in connection with two robberies in four months at the same bank branch, both of which were preceded by diversionary bombings.

The suspects are accused of stealing more than $100,000 in the two attacks, which caused only minor damage and no injuries, but set off a six-month investigation by up to 100 federal agents, FBI Special Agent in Charge Burdena Pasenelli told a news conference.
Spokane County Sheriff John Goldman said the suburban Spokane Valley area where the attacks took place had been "a community under siege" until the arrests.

On April 1 a Spokane newspaper branch office was bombed, and less than 30 minutes later masked gunmen dressed in camouflage fatigues stormed into a nearby U.S. Bank branch, stuffed cash into a duffel bag and set off another explosive device.
In July, a pipe bomb was tossed through the plate-glass door of a Planned Parenthood office shortly before the same bank branch was robbed by three masked men.
Authorities said notes left at the scene and other evidence indicated the men were members of the anti-government white supremacist Phineas Priesthood sect.

On Tuesday FBI agents -- backed by authorities from the Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco and Firearms, the Washington State Patrol, local police and forces from a nearby Army base -- converged on a convenience store in Union Gap, Washington, and arrested the three men, who had stopped for gas.

In their vehicle authorities found a variety of weapons including a grenade, authorities said. They were charged with weapons, explosives, robbery and conspiracy counts that could result in prison sentences of more than 100 years each, a prosecutor said.
In court, no pleas were entered and the men were ordered held pending a bail hearing Tuesday.
